question.problem: The solution to the inequality $-5y+16\le -4$ is $y${{field-1}}{{field-2}}.

current_example.worked_solution:
First, we apply the addition principle, subtracting $3$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x+3 & >-1 \\ -2x+3-3 & >-1-3 \\ -2x+0 & >-4 \\ -2x & >-4\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $-2.$ 

Remember, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x\,\, & >\,\,-4 \\ \frac{-2x}{-2}\, & <\,\,\frac{-4}{-2} \\ \frac{\cancel{-2}x}{\cancel{-2}}\, & <\,\,2 \\ x\,\, & <\,\,2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x<2.$
